question: A 67-year-old woman diagnosed with an infiltrating ductal carcinoma of the breast and no family history of neoplasia. What additional studies should be done on the tumor because of its clinical-therapeutic implications?

options.opa: Complete phenotypic study by flow cytometry.
options.opb: Study of hormonal receptors and HER2.
options.opc: Study of hormonal receptors, ecadherin and study of first degree relatives.
options.opd: BRCA 1-2 study and study of first degree relatives.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Infiltrating ductal carcinoma of the breast -> Hormonal receptors and HER2 study -> 95% CHAIN: Infiltrating ductal carcinoma of the breast -> BRCA1-2 study -> Study of first-degree relatives -> 95%
analysis: In this case of infiltrating ductal carcinoma of the breast in a 67-year-old woman with no family history of neoplasia, the most relevant additional studies would be to assess the hormonal receptors and HER2 status of the tumor. This information is crucial for determining the appropriate targeted therapy and predicting the prognosis of the patient.
